thread:
natalie: Heads up — saw multiple customer streams go into a "stalled" state right after a route flip during the canary. Clients stayed connected but no events for ~12s, then client reconnects after manual page refresh. Console shows a transient drop in streaming_quota_used then a big catch-up spike. No alert fired. :thinking_face:

anya: Can you paste minimal repro steps + any proxy logs?

natalie: Repro on prod-canary: 1) open SSE stream, 2) trigger route swap via canary rollout, 3) proxy returns 204/keepalive, client doesn't attempt resume, ends up re-opening full new connection on user interaction. Logs attached (snippet):
```
proxy: route-change lease=42 -> 43
proxy: socket half-close -> keepalive
proxy: stream-outgoing: paused-for-routing
client: received keepalive (no event)
client: no resume-token present
```

sam: Hmm. sounds like clients are seeing a clean keepalive instead of a terminal close and so they don't trigger resume logic. Why did resume-token disappear?

lucas: FYI deploy-bot showed canary step: deploy-bot: "canary route swap applied to 20% hosts" right before the gaps. Might be sticky routing TTL vs lease reassign.

anya: Do we have a metric distinguishing "paused-by-routing" vs normal idle? If not, console alerting won't catch this pattern.

natalie: No separate metric today. We have streaming_idle and stream_disconnect but not 'stream_paused_for_route'. The console counts look like idle.

sam: Proposal: emit a telemetry label when proxy defers events due to route migration: e.g., stream.transition=route_swap. Then create alert if (transitioned AND no terminal close AND downstream resumed only on UX interaction) > threshold.

lucas: Slight pushback: that could fire for legitimate transient routing moves during autoscaling. We should avoid noisy alerts. Maybe emit a counter and then add a ratio alert: transitions / active_streams > 0.03 over 5m and average resume latency > 5s.

anya: Agreed on ratio. Also add a console UX hint: when a stream resumes with a big token-gap, surface a timeline marker "route swap likely" so SREs can correlate.

natalie: Implementation checklist: (1) proxy: tag events with transition=route_swap or proxy_close; (2) runtime: preserve resume-token across soft handoffs when possible; (3) console: new metric and alert rule + timeline marker; (4) add test for client resume behavior on 204/keepalive.

sam: For (2) note: preserving resume-token requires the lease handoff to copy KV cache pointer. That might be nontrivial across hosts. If we can't copy, maybe issue a short-lived resume-token-ref with central store.

lucas: Central store approach OK but costy. Can we instead change policy to emit a terminal close when we know client can't be continued? That would force immediate client reconnect/resume logic instead of silent pause.

natalie: We tried hard-closing before and it caused spikes of reconnects and higher billing for a subset. Users complained. Need smarter fallback.

anya: Maybe hybrid: try shallow handoff (copy pointer) for high-tier customers; for others use terminal close. That maps to routing policy by customer tier.

sam: Good idea — map to quota/tier. Also add sampling telemetry to see user impact before full rollout.

deploy-bot: Canary step: feature-flag stream.transition-labels enabled on canary hosts (20%).

lucas: I'll prototype the metric and timeline marker this sprint. Natalie, can you capture exact UX repro steps + devtools HAR for the affected customers?

natalie: On it, will DM HARs. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
